chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Bands Tate admired; Benny Carter's band and Marie Cole
summary: He loved Lunceford's reed section and Ellington, James and Dorsey; he discusses why Benny Carter's bands never took off.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Did you listen to other bands then? Were you listening to records? Who mostly?

Well, I used to -- well, I listened to just about -- you know, I listened to all the bands. But I loved Lunceford's reed section. I thought that was one of the prettiest reed sections. And I listened to Duke, I listened to James, Tommy -- I loved Tommy's band -- and I loved them because everybody had a different thing, you know? Everybody had their own thing then. Nobody sounded alike.
Were you aware of Benny Carter's band then?
Did I hear it?
Yeah.
Yeah, I heard it.
That band never really -- why do you think it never --
You know, Benny was like Frankie Trumbauer, never really got off the ground and he's had good bands. It's hard to say just why it really never took --
He had an interesting singer, Leroy Felton.
Yeah, I don't remember him.
He sounded kind of like Eckstine before Eckstine.
Is that right?
Yeah.
Leroy Felton?
On a couple of the records.

Is that right? He's had some good bands. He's a good writer, you know, and he's had some very good bands. Had musicians who were capable of playing his arrangements. I remember he had Marie, when the band -- Marie Cole.
Uh-huh.
She was in the band. And she worked with us, too, before Nat ever -- he hadn't ever seen her then, you know.
Yeah.
She worked with us and she had worked with Benny Carter's band.
